text:
maya: Heads up — multiple customer clusters in eu-west showing a spike of Pending pods. Root cause looks like IP allocation + conntrack exhaustion on GPU node pools. kubelet logs say "failed to assign IP" and kernel spam "nf_conntrack: table full". Autoscaler didn't immediately add capacity because instances are hitting per-node ENI/IP limits. Anyone digging in?

sam: yep saw it. quick logs from one node:```
May 12 10:03:12 ip-10-0-12-34 kubelet[1234]: failed to allocate IP from aws-vpc-cni: no available addresses
May 12 10:03:13 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
May 12 10:03:15 kubelet[1234]: pod mymodel-0 Pending: failed to assign IP
```

oliver: sounds like aws-cni + ENI ceiling. On p4d / p3 instances you get limited ENIs and IPs per ENI so high pod density -> exhausted. Also conntrack fills when many short-lived connections (inference bursts). We should both increase conntrack table and reduce per-node IP pressure.

tess: quick proposals:
- bump nf_conntrack_max via sysctl on node pool bootstrap (Terraform user_data or node taint init)
- tune aws-vpc-cni: set WARM_IP_TARGET/WARM_ENI_TARGET or enable prefix delegation so CNI pre-warms IPs
- change autoscaler helm values to prefer many smaller GPU nodes or mixed instance types (improves IP density)

maya: +1. I'm worried about changing instance types mid-heap, we should prefer short-term sysctl + CNI warm targets and a longer-term plan to add a warm pool. Also autoscaler max_node_provision_time was defaulting to 40m in our helm values which slows fallback.

sam: sysctl check command I ran: `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` and `conntrack -S`. Current nodes at ~128k, conntrack_count at ~125k when we hit the issue. Quick mitigation: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` and `echo 524288 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` then monitor.

oliver: terraform/helm bits I think we should change: add extra sysctl via node pool module + update aws-node helm chart envs. Example snippets:```hcl
module "gpu_nodepool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/modules/k8s-nodepool.git//aws"
  name = "gpu-eu-west-1"
  instance_type = "g5.12xlarge"
  min_size = 2
  max_size = 12
  node_labels = { role = "gpu" }
  extra_user_data = file("bootstrap-sysctl.sh") # sets nf_conntrack_max
}
```
and Helm values for aws-node / aws-cni:```yaml
aws-node:
  env:
    - name: WARM_IP_TARGET
      value: "30"
    - name: WARM_ENI_TARGET
      value: "2"
    - name: ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION
      value: "true"
```
and cluster-autoscaler values:```yaml
clusterAutoscaler:
  extraArgs:
    max-node-provision-time: "15m"
    expander: "least-waste"
  podAnnotations:
    cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"
```

tess: I also recommend adding a warm node pool (reserved capacity) specifically for GPU bursts — cheaper than overprovisioning whole fleet and faster than cold provisioning on spot. Terraform example:```hcl
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu_warm" {
  cluster_name = var.cluster
  node_group_name = "gpu-warm"
  scaling_config { desired_size = 1 min_size = 1 max_size = 2 }
  labels = { warmpool = "true" }
  tags = { billing = "reserved-burst" }
}
```

maya: infra-bot just posted helm upgrade for cluster-autoscaler in staging, heads-up: `infra-bot: deployed cluster-autoscaler v1.22.0 to staging with max-node-provision-time=15m` :robot_face:

oliver: action items I propose:
1) apply sysctl bump to affected nodepools (short-term) — owner: sam
2) change aws-node helm env in a canary (staging) to WARM_IP_TARGET=30 — owner: maya
3) open Terraform PR for gpu nodepool bootstrap script that sets conntrack and documents ENI/IP limits, plus optional warm pool — owner: maya
4) evaluate splitting GPU workload into smaller instance types to increase IP density — owner: tess

sam: I'll run `conntrack -L | wc -l` on affected nodes and flush small connections after we apply sysctl. Will also add monitoring alert for conntrack util > 80%

maya: I'll open the TF PR and link to this thread. Thanks all — will monitor once staging helm change lands.

infra-bot: reminder: please add a changelog entry for the cluster-autoscaler/helm tweak and tag the PR with `eng-infra`.
